bull.t: Initial Revenue and Proven Yield Mechanism
bull.b: Gold-lease income and four scheduled distributions show the core yield mechanism has moved beyond concept to initial repeatable operation. That proof supports future monetization as GLDY activity and assets under management expand, although current contribution remains small.

Reducing operating expenses by 57.1% and sharply narrowing quarterly losses demonstrates management can reset the cost base while commercialization develops. Lower recurring spending should extend runway and reduce the revenue scale required to approach sustainability, despite continued losses.

bull.t: Debt-Free Balance Sheet and Liquidity Runway
bull.b: No debt, $32.8M of working capital and $41.8M of total liquidity provide flexibility to fund product development and integrations without immediate borrowing. Management estimates immediately available funds cover about 18 months and total liquidity about three years assuming no new revenue.

bear.t: Revenue Remains Far Below the Cost Base
bear.b: Quarterly gold-lease revenue of only $134k-$146k remains immaterial against the $15.2M operating loss, while TTM revenue is about $0.15M. The business therefore has not yet demonstrated sufficient commercial scale or margin absorption to support its cost base.

bear.t: Limited Adoption and Concentrated Institutional Dependence
bear.b: GLDY AUM was about 3.1k ounces and roughly 9% was held externally, with growth dependent on a forthcoming concentrated institutional allocation. This narrow adoption base makes expansion reliant on counterparties completing diligence and converting planned partnerships into holders.

Material weaknesses disclosed in the 2025 annual report remained unremediated at June 30, 2026, and disclosure controls were deemed ineffective. Persistent control gaps can hinder reliable reporting and institutional confidence while the company scales its partnership-based platform.
